audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet final Jerusalem siege, Zedekiah capture and blinding, temple and city destruction, executions and exile, Gedaliah governorship and assassination, flight to Egypt, and Jehoiachin release narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for siege chronology, famine, military flight, Zedekiah's capture, killing of his sons before him, blinding and restraints, urban and temple burning, wall destruction, mass deportation, poor agricultural laborers left, cultural extraction, Riblah executions, colonial governorship, political assassination, refugee flight to Egypt, and Jehoiachin's limited elevation in Babylon.

verses.restored: In ninth year of his reign, in tenth month, on tenth of month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem. He camped against it and built siege works around it.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he, and all his host, against Jerusalem, and pitched against it; and they built forts against it round about.

verses.restored: City entered siege until eleventh year of king Zedekiah.

familiar.text: And the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.

verses.restored: On ninth of fourth month famine was strong in city, and there was no bread for people of land.

familiar.text: And on the ninth day of the fourth month the famine prevailed in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

verses.restored: City was breached, and all men of war fled by night by way of gate between two walls by king's garden, while Chaldeans surrounded city. The king went by way toward Arabah.

familiar.text: And the city was broken up, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls, which is by the king’s garden: (now the Chaldees were against the city round about:) and the king went the way toward the plain.

verses.restored: Army of Chaldeans pursued king and overtook him in plains of Jericho; all his army scattered from him.

familiar.text: And the army of the Chaldees pursued after the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho: and all his army were scattered from him.

verses.restored: They seized king and brought him up to king of Babylon at Riblah, and they spoke judgments against him.

familiar.text: So they took the king, and brought him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah; and they gave judgment upon him.

verses.restored: They slaughtered sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; then they blinded eyes of Zedekiah, bound him with bronze restraints, and brought him to Babylon.

familiar.text: And they slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon.

verses.restored: In fifth month, on seventh of month, which was nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan chief of guards, servant of king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which is the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, unto Jerusalem:

verses.restored: He burned house of YHWH, king's house, and all houses of Jerusalem; every great house he burned with fire.

familiar.text: And he burnt the house of the LORD, and the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great man’s house burnt he with fire.

verses.restored: All army of Chaldeans with chief of guards tore down walls around Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And all the army of the Chaldees, that were with the captain of the guard, brake down the walls of Jerusalem round about.

verses.restored: Remaining people left in city, deserters who had fallen to king of Babylon, and rest of multitude, Nebuzaradan chief of guards exiled.

familiar.text: Now the rest of the people that were left in the city, and the fugitives that fell away to the king of Babylon, with the remnant of the multitude, did Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carry away.

verses.restored: But chief of guards left some of poorest of land as vineyard workers and field workers.

familiar.text: But the captain of the guard left of the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen.

verses.restored: Bronze pillars in house of YHWH, stands, and bronze sea in house of YHWH Chaldeans broke apart and carried their bronze to Babylon.

familiar.text: And the pillars of brass that were in the house of the LORD, and the bases, and the brasen sea that was in the house of the LORD, did the Chaldees break in pieces, and carried the brass of them to Babylon.

verses.restored: Pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and all bronze vessels with which they ministered, they took.

familiar.text: And the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass wherewith they ministered, took they away.

verses.restored: Firepans and bowls—what was gold as gold and what was silver as silver—chief of guards took.

familiar.text: And the firepans, and the bowls, and such things as were of gold, in gold, and of silver, in silver, the captain of the guard took away.

verses.restored: Two pillars, one sea, and stands Solomon made for house of YHWH—the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weighing.

familiar.text: The two pillars, one sea, and the bases which Solomon had made for the house of the LORD; the brass of all these vessels was without weight.

verses.restored: Height of one pillar was eighteen cubits, and capital upon it was bronze; height of capital was three cubits, with lattice and pomegranates upon capital all around, all bronze. Like these was second pillar with lattice.

familiar.text: The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and the chapiter upon it was brass: and the height of the chapiter three cubits; and the wreathen work, and pomegranates upon the chapiter round about, all of brass: and like unto these had the second pillar with wreathen work.

verses.restored: Chief of guards took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah second priest, and three guardians of threshold.

familiar.text: And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door:

verses.restored: From city he took one officer appointed over men of war, five men seeing face of king who were found in city, scribe of commander of army who mustered people of land, and sixty men from people of land found in city.

familiar.text: And out of the city he took an officer that was set over the men of war, and five men of them that were in the king’s presence, which were found in the city, and the principal scribe of the host, which mustered the people of the land, and threescore men of the people of the land that were found in the city:

verses.restored: Nebuzaradan chief of guards took them and brought them to king of Babylon at Riblah.

familiar.text: And Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took these, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah:

verses.restored: King of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Riblah in land of Hamath. Thus Judah was exiled from upon its land.

familiar.text: And the king of Babylon smote them, and slew them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried away out of their land.

verses.restored: Over people remaining in land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon left, he appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan.

familiar.text: And as for the people that remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, even over them he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, ruler.

verses.restored: All commanders of armies, they and their men, heard that king of Babylon appointed Gedaliah. They came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of Maacathite, they and their men.

familiar.text: And when all the captains of the armies, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor, there came to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan the son of Careah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of a Maachathite, they and their men.

verses.restored: Gedaliah swore to them and their men and said to them, Do not fear servants of Chaldeans. Live in land, serve king of Babylon, and it will be well for you.

familiar.text: And Gedaliah sware to them, and to their men, and said unto them, Fear not to be the servants of the Chaldees: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon; and it shall be well with you.

verses.restored: In seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, from royal seed, came, and ten men with him. They struck Gedaliah, and he died, along with Judeans and Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.

familiar.text: But it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, came, and ten men with him, and smote Gedaliah, that he died, and the Jews and the Chaldees that were with him at Mizpah.

verses.restored: All people, from small to great, and commanders of armies arose and came to Egypt, for they feared Chaldeans.

familiar.text: And all the people, both small and great, and the captains of the armies, arose, and came to Egypt: for they were afraid of the Chaldees.

verses.restored: In thirty-seventh year of exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in twelfth month, on twenty-seventh of month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in year he became king, lifted head of Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the seven and twentieth day of the month, that Evilmerodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison;

verses.restored: He spoke good things with him and set his throne above thrones of kings who were with him in Babylon.

familiar.text: And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon;

verses.restored: He changed garments of his imprisonment, and Jehoiachin ate bread continually before him all days of his life.

familiar.text: And changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life.

verses.restored: His allowance was a continual allowance given to him from king, a day's portion in its day, all days of his life.

familiar.text: And his allowance was a continual allowance given him of the king, a daily rate for every day, all the days of his life.

translation_notes: The siege lasts into a devastating famine. Starvation is a weapon and consequence of war, not proof that hungry civilians lacked faith or deserved suffering.
Zedekiah's sons are killed before his eyes, then he is blinded and restrained. This is torture designed to combine bereavement, sensory injury, humiliation, and captivity.
Blindness and disability are not the shame in verse 7; deliberate mutilation and imperial cruelty are. Disabled people must never be used as symbols of moral blindness or ruined masculinity.
Burning temple, palace, and homes and destroying city walls are cultural, religious, domestic, and civic devastation—not merely fulfillment or architectural change.
Those left as vineyard and field workers are called poorest of land. They retain full dignity and become coerced survivors responsible for food production amid destroyed institutions.
Temple bronze and vessels are dismantled and transferred. Material detail preserves the scale of cultural extraction and the loss of collective craft heritage.
Priests, officials, military personnel, a scribe, and sixty people are transported to Riblah and executed. Captive killing without due process remains atrocity.
Gedaliah governs under Babylonian appointment. His advice may be pragmatic survival under occupation, not free political consent or endorsement of empire.
Ishmael's royal descent does not legitimate assassination. His killing of Gedaliah, Judeans, and Chaldeans destabilizes the surviving community.
The flight to Egypt is refugee movement caused by credible fear of imperial reprisal. Displaced people must not be condemned for seeking safety.
Jehoiachin's release, changed clothing, table access, and daily allowance improve one prisoner's conditions but do not end exile, empire, dependence, or the suffering of the wider community.
Kings, Jeremiah, Chronicles, Ezekiel, and Babylonian evidence contain chronological and numerical differences requiring source-witness audit.
safety_note: Do not romanticize siege, starvation, child killing, blinding, cultural destruction, captive execution, occupation, assassination, or exile. Do not stigmatize disability or poverty, and do not condemn refugees who flee to Egypt. The book ends with limited dignity restored to one prisoner—not with empire defeated or collective trauma resolved.
